name: aws-container
description: An API backend running a standard HTTP server in containers — ECS/Fargate + ALB + RDS PostgreSQL + Drizzle + Cognito (OIDC). Designed so AWS dependence stays in the infrastructure layer only and the system can move on-premises.

notes.securityBoundary: **There is no row-level policy engine.** The DB is reached over a trusted connection, so there is no data-layer enforcement like RLS and the application-layer ownership check is the only boundary. Carrying the BaaS combination's 'the data layer backs you up' wording over verbatim produces **exactly the opposite guidance** — every read and mutation query must carry an ownership filter, and a 0-row mutation must not be answered as a success
notes.serverCodeLocation: The container API server in this repository. The frontend is an SPA with no server runtime, so this backend owns all server logic
notes.portability: **Design on the premise of an on-premises move.** Keep AWS dependence in the infrastructure layer only and keep application code vendor-neutral: a standard HTTP server (the same image runs on K8s and on-premises Docker) · RDS PostgreSQL (avoid Aurora-only features) · authentication by standard OIDC/JWKS verification (no direct dependence on the Cognito SDK — swap issuer and JWKS URL to move to Keycloak) · file storage against the S3 API with a configurable endpoint (MinIO-compatible) · logs as structured JSON on stdout (no CloudWatch SDK) · configuration through env as the single entry point (Secrets Manager is only an injection mechanism). **The guide explicitly separates which AWS services touch app code and which stay in the infrastructure layer**
notes.dataModeling: Relational PostgreSQL, so the T1 data-modeling card is **active** (`paths:` includes `drizzle/**` · `db/**` · `**/migrations/**`). Do not copy the card; reference it by naming the real paths
notes.localParity: `docker compose` brings up PostgreSQL locally in exactly the same shape — being able to actually run and verify migrations and integration tests is the core advantage of this combination, so the test slot is written on that premise
notes.variants: For serverless (Lambda + API Gateway + DynamoDB) there is a separate `aws-serverless` preset — there, on top of the missing row-level policy engine, connection pooling and cold starts become the central topics
